experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Trek through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and glacial moraines while enjoying breathtaking views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and surrounding Himalayan peaks. The trail passes through traditional Gurung villages offering authentic cultural encounters along the way.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of Nepal's most spectacular sunrises. Watch golden light illuminate the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges in a stunning panoramic display. The 2-hour ascent from Ghorepani is manageable for most fitness levels and rewards hikers with unforgettable 180-degree Himalayan views.

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Homestay
experiences.description: Spend a night in a traditional Gurung family home in the village of Ghandruk, one of the largest Gurung settlements in Nepal. Share home-cooked dal bhat, learn about indigenous shamanic traditions, explore the Gurung Museum, and witness traditional weaving and farming practices. This immersive experience provides deep insight into Himalayan mountain culture.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal High Camp Trek
experiences.description: Explore the less-crowded Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering stunning close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain) and the Annapurna massif. Trek through dense forests of oak and rhododendron, spot Himalayan wildlife including langur monkeys and colorful pheasants, and reach the high camp at 4,500m for extraordinary solitude and panoramic vistas.

experiences.name: Pokhara Lakeside Nature and Food Tour
experiences.description: Begin your Annapurna adventure with a guided nature walk along Phewa Lake in Pokhara, the gateway city to the Annapurna region. Visit the World Peace Pagoda for panoramic mountain reflections on the lake, then explore the vibrant Lakeside bazaar sampling local Newari and Thakali cuisine including sel roti, thukpa noodle soup, and freshly brewed tongba millet beer at local teahouses.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, exchange currency at the airport (better rates available in Thamel). Take a prepaid taxi or public bus to Thamel (~NPR 700-1000 by taxi or NPR 50-80 by local bus). Check into a budget guesthouse in Thamel and freshen up. Begin permit preparations: visit the Nepal Tourism Board office (closes 17:00) to obtain your TIMS card (NPR 2000 for SAARC, NPR 3000 for others) and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit/ACAP (NPR 3000). Stroll through Thamel to get oriented and purchase any last-minute trekking gear from budget shops.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Thamel's vibrant streets on foot. Visit a local gear shop to stock up on snacks, energy bars, and water purification tablets for the trek. Relax and plan the upcoming days over dinner.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat set meal at a local Thamel restaurant (~NPR 300-400) — filling and budget-friendly
meals.dinner: Thakali Kitchen or similar local Nepali restaurant in Thamel for Dal Bhat or momos (~NPR 350-500)

day_by_day.notes: Priority on Day 1 is obtaining both the TIMS card and ACAP permit before offices close. Keep all permit documents safe throughout the trek. Exchange enough cash (NPR) as ATMs become scarce beyond Pokhara. Budget guesthouses in Thamel cost NPR 500-1000/night.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast in Thamel. Head to Kathmandu's Gongabu Bus Park or book a tourist bus from Thamel to Pokhara (NPR 500-800 for tourist bus, departs around 07:00-08:00, ~7-8 hours). Alternatively, take a local bus for NPR 300-400. Enjoy the scenic mountain highway views as you travel west through the Prithvi Highway along the Trishuli and Marsyangdi river valleys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara by mid-afternoon (around 14:00-15:00). Check into a budget guesthouse in Lakeside (Baidam) area — rooms available from NPR 600-1200/night. Drop bags and head to Lakeside for a short orientation walk along Phewa Lake. Visit a local trekking shop to confirm you have all necessary gear: trekking poles, rain gear, and a good sleeping bag (can rent sleeping bags for ~NPR 100-150/day).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Phewa Lake from the lakeside promenade — free and spectacular. Stroll along the Lakeside strip and browse local shops. Enjoy dinner with views of the lake.

meals.breakfast: Bread, eggs, and tea at a Thamel bakery (~NPR 200-300)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from Thamel or stop at a roadside dhaba along the highway (~NPR 200-300)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta at a budget lakeside restaurant in Pokhara (~NPR 350-500)

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets the evening before from a Thamel travel agent to secure a seat. Tourist buses are more comfortable but local buses are cheaper. Confirm your trekking gear checklist: waterproof jacket, sturdy trekking boots, warm layers, headlamp, and first aid kit. Pokhara is the last major city before the trek begins.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise view of the Annapurna and Machapuchare (Fishtail) peaks from Pokhara — best viewed from the lakeside or Peace Stupa hill. After breakfast, organize your pack: leave non-essential luggage at your guesthouse (most offer free storage). Take a local bus or shared jeep from Pokhara's Baglung Bus Park to Nayapul (NPR 200-300, ~1.5 hours). Begin the trek from Nayapul, crossing the Modi Khola suspension bridge and trekking through terraced fields and rhododendron forests toward Tikhedhunga.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga upward on the stone-paved trail. Climb the famous 3,000+ stone steps to Ulleri (elevation ~1,960m). This is a challenging but rewarding ascent through dense forest. Rest at Ulleri and take in panoramic views of the Modi Khola Valley and surrounding peaks. Check into a basic teahouse/lodge (~NPR 200-400/night, often free with meal purchase).
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse in Ulleri. Chat with fellow trekkers and share route tips. Enjoy the cool mountain air and clear October skies ideal for stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs and toast at Pokhara guesthouse (~NPR 200-350)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga (~NPR 350-450)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Ulleri teahouse (~NPR 400-500) — always the best value on the trail

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — trails will be busy but weather is excellent. Trekking distance today: approximately 10-12 km, 5-6 hours. The Ulleri stone staircase is steep — take your time and stay hydrated. Teahouse accommodation is basic (shared bathrooms common) but clean and warm.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Ulleri. Trek through magnificent rhododendron and oak forests toward Ghorepani (elevation ~2,860m). The trail is relatively gentle after yesterday's climb. Pass through Banthanti and Nangethanti villages, enjoying the forest canopy and occasional views of Annapurna South. Arrive in Ghorepani by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a teahouse in Ghorepani and drop your pack. Afternoon hike up to Poon Hill (elevation ~3,210m) for afternoon views — or save this for the famous sunrise the next morning. Alternatively, explore Ghorepani village, interact with local Magar and Gurung communities, and visit the small local shops. Rest and acclimatize to the altitude.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ghorepani teahouse for a warm dinner. The evenings in Ghorepani get cold in October (~5-10°C) — layer up. Socialize in the teahouse common room with other trekkers over hot tea and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and tea at Ulleri teahouse (~NPR 300-400)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and bread or fried rice at Banthanti (~NPR 350-450)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with vegetable curry at Ghorepani teahouse (~NPR 400-550)

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: approximately 9-11 km, 4-5 hours. Altitude gain is significant today — drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol. Ghorepani has multiple teahouses competing for business; negotiate room rates especially if you agree to eat all meals there. Set an alarm for 04:30 for tomorrow's Poon Hill sunrise.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 04:30 and hike up to Poon Hill (45-60 minutes) to catch the legendary sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. On a clear October morning, you'll see Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machapuchare (6,993m) bathed in golden light — one of the most iconic mountain panoramas in the world. Small entry fee (~NPR 100) applies at the viewpoint. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: After breakfast, trek from Ghorepani toward Tadapani (elevation ~2,630m) via the ridge trail through dense rhododendron forest. The trail offers continuous mountain views. Pass through Deurali and descend through forest to Tadapani. Check into a teahouse and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of Tadapani — a quieter stop than Ghorepani. Watch the alpenglow on Machapuchare and Annapurna South at sunset from the village viewpoint. Early dinner and rest for the long day ahead.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or eggs with tea after returning from Poon Hill (~NPR 300-400)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a teahouse along the Deurali trail (~NPR 350-450)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Tadapani teahouse (~NPR 400-500)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill sunrise in October is spectacular but popular — arrive early to secure a good viewing spot. Trekking distance today (including Poon Hill): approximately 12-14 km, 5-6 hours. The Ghorepani-Tadapani ridge trail is one of the most beautiful sections of the Annapurna region. Carry warm layers for the pre-dawn Poon Hill hike.

day_by_day.morning: Morning views of Machapuchare from Tadapani are outstanding — spend 30 minutes at the viewpoint before breakfast. Trek from Tadapani down through rhododendron and bamboo forest toward Chhomrong (elevation ~2,170m), a major Gurung village and key gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary. The trail descends steeply to the Kimrong Khola river and climbs back up to Chhomrong — a challenging but rewarding section.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong and check into a teahouse. Explore this well-established Gurung village: visit the local school, small monastery, and community viewpoints. Chhomrong has some of the best-equipped teahouses on the route with hot showers available (~NPR 200-300 extra). Take a short walk to the upper village for panoramic views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli directly ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Chhomrong is a social hub on the trail. Chat with trekkers heading both up and down the valley for current trail conditions. The teahouse owners here are wonderfully hospitable — ask about local Gurung culture and traditions over dinner.

meals.breakfast: Muesli with hot milk or eggs at Tadapani teahouse (~NPR 300-400)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or pasta at a teahouse near Kimrong Khola (~NPR 350-500)
meals.dinner: Gurung bread (Dhido) with vegetable curry or Dal Bhat at Chhomrong teahouse (~NPR 400-550)

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: approximately 10-12 km, 5-6 hours. Chhomrong marks the official entry to the Annapurna Sanctuary — ensure your ACAP permit is ready for checkpoint inspection. Water purification is essential from here onward — use iodine tablets or a filter rather than buying plastic bottles. Stock up on snacks in Chhomrong as prices increase higher up.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down the long stone staircase to Chhomrong Khola river (elevation ~1,950m) and begin the ascent toward Sinuwa (elevation ~2,360m). Pass through bamboo and rhododendron forest. The trail enters the increasingly narrow Modi Khola Valley with towering walls of Hiunchuli and Machapuchare closing in on both sides — a dramatic and immersive landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Sinuwa through dense bamboo forest to Bamboo (elevation ~2,310m) and onward to Dovan (elevation ~2,600m). The forest is lush and atmospheric, with the sound of the Modi Khola river below. Look out for Himalayan Tahr, langur monkeys, and various bird species including Danphe (Himalayan Monal), Nepal's national bird. Check into a teahouse at Dovan.
day_by_day.evening: Dovan is a small, quiet settlement with just a few teahouses. Enjoy the solitude and the sound of the river. The valley walls are dramatic in the evening light. Rest well — altitude increases significantly over the next two days.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with banana and tea at Chhomrong teahouse (~NPR 300-400)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and fried noodles at Sinuwa or Bamboo (~NPR 350-500)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Dovan teahouse (~NPR 450-600) — note prices increase with altitude

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: approximately 10-12 km, 5-6 hours. Altitude sickness awareness begins here. Drink 3-4 liters of water daily, avoid alcohol, and report any severe headaches, nausea, or dizziness to fellow trekkers or teahouse owners. Garlic soup is a traditional altitude remedy on this trail. Teahouse options become more limited from here — accommodation is simple but adequate.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan through increasingly dramatic gorge scenery. Pass Himalaya Hotel (elevation ~2,920m) — a well-known teahouse stop. The valley narrows dramatically as you approach the entrance to the Annapurna Sanctuary. Trek through Hinku Cave (a natural rock overhang used as shelter) and Deurali (elevation ~3,230m). The landscape transitions from forest to high alpine terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the avalanche-prone section between Deurali and the Sanctuary entrance — move efficiently through this area and follow local guidance. Enter the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) approach trail with the full 360-degree amphitheater of peaks beginning to reveal itself. Arrive at Machapuchare Base Camp/MBC (elevation ~3,700m) — a stunning location with Machapuchare's perfect pyramid directly above. Check into a teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: The views from MBC at sunset are extraordinary — Machapuchare, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, and Annapurna III surround you in a complete mountain amphitheater. Spend the evening stargazing — at this altitude with minimal light pollution, the Milky Way is breathtaking. It will be cold (~0-5°C) — use your sleeping bag liner.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast with hot lemon tea at Dovan (~NPR 350-450)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and pasta at Himalaya Hotel (~NPR 450-600)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or hot noodle soup at MBC teahouse (~NPR 500-700) — portions are generous for altitude

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: approximately 10-12 km, 5-6 hours. Altitude gain is significant today (over 1,000m from Dovan). Walk slowly, breathe deeply, and take regular breaks. October weather is generally stable but afternoon clouds can roll in — aim to reach MBC by 14:00. Temperatures drop sharply after sunset. Teahouse blankets are available but sleeping bags are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from MBC (06:00) to reach Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, elevation ~4,130m) for sunrise — one of the most spectacular mountain experiences in the world. The 2-hour climb from MBC to ABC in the pre-dawn cold is absolutely worth it. At ABC, you stand in the heart of the Annapurna Sanctuary, completely surrounded by 7,000-8,000m peaks. Watch the sunrise paint Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Gangapurna, and Machapuchare in shades of orange, pink, and gold.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning at ABC exploring the sanctuary floor, visiting the Annapurna Base Camp memorial chortens, and absorbing the incredible 360-degree mountain panorama. Take photographs, journal, and simply sit in awe. This is the highlight of the entire trek. Begin the descent back to MBC for lunch, then continue descending to Dovan or Bamboo to assist with acclimatization.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Bamboo or Sinuwa for the night. The descent feels fast after the long climb up — your legs and lungs will appreciate the lower altitude. Celebrate reaching ABC over a well-earned dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and tea before departing MBC (~NPR 350-450)
meals.lunch: Soup and fried rice at MBC or on descent (~NPR 500-650)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with extra portions at Bamboo or Sinuwa teahouse (~NPR 400-550)

day_by_day.notes: ABC at 4,130m — this is the highest point of the trek. Altitude sickness is a real risk: if you experience severe headache, vomiting, or loss of coordination, descend immediately. October skies are typically crystal clear in the morning — afternoon clouds are common. The descent from ABC to lower altitudes is important for health. Trekking distance today: approximately 14-16 km total.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-rested night at lower altitude, begin the descent from Bamboo/Sinuwa back toward Chhomrong. The trail back through the bamboo forest feels familiar but beautiful from the opposite direction. Take time to appreciate the forest details — mosses, ferns, orchids, and birdlife — that you may have rushed past on the ascent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Chhomrong for lunch. Treat yourself to a hot shower (NPR 200-300) — well deserved after days on the trail. Rest in Chhomrong for the afternoon. Revisit the village viewpoints for a final look at Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Chat with upward-bound trekkers and share your experience of ABC.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Chhomrong — you've completed the Annapurna Sanctuary trek! Enjoy apple pie or chocolate cake, a Chhomrong specialty, for dessert. Rest well for the continued descent tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or eggs at Bamboo/Sinuwa teahouse (~NPR 300-400)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or pizza (yes, teahouses in Chhomrong serve it!) at Chhomrong (~NPR 400-600)
meals.dinner: Thakali set meal or Dal Bhat with apple pie dessert at Chhomrong teahouse (~NPR 500-700)

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: approximately 10-12 km, 5-6 hours. Your knees will feel the descent today — trekking poles are invaluable on the steep Chhomrong staircase. Take care on wet stone steps. Chhomrong is a great place to buy locally produced honey and Gurung handicrafts as affordable souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back toward Ghandruk (elevation ~1,940m) via a scenic trail through the Modi Khola Valley. This route passes through Kimrong village and offers stunning views of Machapuchare and the Annapurna range from a completely different angle. Ghandruk is one of the largest and most beautiful Gurung villages in Nepal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghandruk and explore this remarkable stone-paved village. Visit the Gurung Museum (entry ~NPR 100) to learn about Gurung culture, traditions, and the famous Gurkha military history. Walk the traditional stone lanes between traditional slate-roofed houses with flower-filled windows. The views of Annapurna South and Machapuchare from Ghandruk's upper village are spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Ghandruk has excellent teahouses with rooftop terraces perfect for evening mountain watching. The village atmosphere is warm and welcoming. Enjoy a traditional Gurung cultural evening if a local cultural program is running (sometimes organized by teahouses, ~NPR 200-300).

meals.breakfast: Porridge and hot lemon tea at Chhomrong teahouse (~NPR 300-400)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a trail teahouse (~NPR 350-450)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with local Gurung-style vegetable curry at Ghandruk teahouse (~NPR 400-550)

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: approximately 8-10 km, 4-5 hours. Ghandruk is a highlight of the Annapurna region — take time to explore beyond just passing through. The village has reliable WiFi at some teahouses (~NPR 100-200) if you want to share your trek photos. October evenings in Ghandruk are cool and clear — perfect for stargazing from the rooftop terrace.

day_by_day.morning: Morning sunrise from Ghandruk's upper viewpoint — Annapurna South and Machapuchare glow at dawn. After breakfast, trek from Ghandruk down to Kimche and then to Nayapul via the lower Modi Khola Valley trail. The descent passes through terraced rice fields (October harvest season — golden fields everywhere), small farming villages, and suspension bridges over the Modi Khola river.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul by early afternoon. Take a local jeep or bus back to Pokhara (NPR 200-300, ~1.5 hours). Check back into your Lakeside guesthouse. Treat yourself to a long hot shower, laundry service (~NPR 100-150/kg), and rest. Spend the late afternoon strolling along Phewa Lake — it will feel luxurious after the trek.
day_by_day.evening: Pokhara celebration dinner! You've completed the Annapurna Sanctuary trek. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal at a lakeside restaurant — still budget-friendly but a step up from teahouse food. Watch the reflection of lights on Phewa Lake.

meals.breakfast: Eggs, toast, and fresh juice at Ghandruk teahouse (~NPR 300-450)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at a trail teahouse near Kimche (~NPR 350-450)
meals.dinner: Nepali thali or continental meal at a Pokhara lakeside restaurant (~NPR 500-800) — splurge slightly for the celebration!

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: approximately 8-10 km to Nayapul, 4-5 hours. The jeep from Nayapul to Pokhara runs frequently — no need to pre-book. Back in Pokhara, visit a pharmacy if you need any medical supplies or altitude medication refills. Consider booking a massage (~NPR 500-800/hour) to recover your trekking muscles.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara — well deserved! Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast with lake views. Morning boat ride on Phewa Lake to the Tal Barahi Temple (island temple) — rent a rowboat for ~NPR 500-700/hour or take the short ferry (~NPR 30). The reflections of the Annapurna range in the lake on a clear October morning are breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (entry NPR 400) — a world-class museum dedicated to Himalayan mountaineering history, featuring exhibits on all 14 eight-thousanders and the climbers who conquered them. Great context after your own Annapurna experience. Alternatively, hike up to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic views of Pokhara, Phewa Lake, and the entire Annapurna range (free entry, 45-minute hike from lakeside).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Pokhara — explore the Lakeside market for souvenirs: Pashmina scarves (~NPR 500-1500), Thangka paintings, prayer flags, and locally made trekking accessories. Enjoy a farewell dinner at Lakeside with fellow trekkers you've met on the trail.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast with fresh fruit, eggs, and coffee at a Lakeside café (~NPR 400-600)
meals.lunch: Momos (dumplings) and butter tea at a local Tibetan restaurant in Pokhara (~NPR 250-400)
meals.dinner: Newari-style feast or Thakali kitchen set meal at a recommended Pokhara restaurant (~NPR 500-700)

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara is one of Nepal's most beautiful cities — take time to simply relax and enjoy it. Book your return bus to Kathmandu for tomorrow morning from a Lakeside travel agent (~NPR 500-800 for tourist bus). Organize your luggage: pack trekking gear separately from items you'll need in Kathmandu. October weather in Pokhara is typically sunny and warm (~22-25°C during the day).

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast before the bus departs. Take the tourist bus from Pokhara back to Kathmandu (departs ~07:00-08:00, NPR 500-800, ~7-8 hours). Enjoy the scenic Prithvi Highway journey one final time — the mountain views near Dumre and the Trishuli River gorge are beautiful. Alternatively, take a domestic flight from Pokhara to Kathmandu (Buddha Air/Yeti Airlines, ~30 minutes, ~NPR 4,000-6,000) for spectacular aerial views of the Himalayas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kathmandu. Check into a Thamel guesthouse if you have an overnight stay, or head to the airport for onward travel. If time permits, visit Boudhanath Stupa (UNESCO World Heritage Site, entry NPR 400) — the largest stupa in Nepal and a magnificent Buddhist monument surrounded by monasteries. Or visit Pashupatinath Temple complex on the Bagmati River.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Nepal — stroll through Thamel for last-minute shopping: Nepali teas, spices, prayer wheels, and handicrafts. Enjoy a farewell Nepali dinner at a traditional restaurant. Reflect on an incredible 14-day journey through one of the world's most spectacular mountain landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Pokhara guesthouse before bus (~NPR 200-300)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the bus or stop at a highway dhaba (~NPR 200-350)
meals.dinner: Traditional Nepali thali at a Thamel restaurant (~NPR 400-600) — final Dal Bhat of the trip!

day_by_day.notes: Total approximate budget breakdown for 14 days: Permits (TIMS + ACAP): NPR 5,000-6,000 | Transport (buses + local): NPR 2,000-3,000 | Accommodation (14 nights): NPR 5,000-10,000 | Food (14 days): NPR 15,000-20,000 | Miscellaneous (gear rental, entry fees, tips): NPR 3,000-5,000 | TOTAL: approximately NPR 30,000-44,000 (USD 225-330). Tip your teahouse hosts and trekking guides generously — even NPR 500-1,000 is meaningful. October is the best month to trek in Nepal — you've chosen perfectly!

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Modi Khola Valley Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and transfer to your pre-booked hotel in Pokhara via tourist bus or private vehicle (approx. 6–7 hours) or take a 25-minute domestic flight to Pokhara if available. Settle into a mid-range guesthouse in Pokhara's Lakeside district for the night before the trek begins.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Phewa Lake's Lakeside promenade, browse trekking gear shops to pick up any last-minute supplies, and enjoy a relaxed orientation walk around Lakeside Pokhara.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick snack at Kathmandu airport
meals.lunch: Light meal at a roadside dhaba or airport café during transit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Moondance Restaurant or Caffe Concerto in Pokhara Lakeside — try dal bhat or pasta, budget NPR 600–1,000

day_by_day.notes: Book a domestic flight Kathmandu–Pokhara in advance if preferred over the bus. Keep trekking permits (TIMS Card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) ready to obtain in Pokhara the next morning. Rest well — acclimatization starts now.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Pokhara trekking permit office to obtain your TIMS Card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP). Then drive or take a local bus to Nayapul (1.5–2 hours) — the traditional trek starting point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the trek from Nayapul (1,070 m) through Birethanti and along the Modi Khola river valley. Trek through lush subtropical forests and terraced farmland to reach Tikhedhunga (1,540 m) — approximately 3–4 hours of moderate hiking.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tikhedhunga, check into a comfortable teahouse, freshen up, and relax on the terrace overlooking the river gorge. Watch the sunset paint the hills golden.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at your Pokhara guesthouse — eggs, toast, and tea, NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Birethanti, NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice and lentil soup at Tikhedhunga teahouse, NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Wear broken-in trekking boots from day one. Carry at least 2 liters of water. The trail from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga is well-marked and relatively easy — a good warm-up day.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and tackle the famous 3,340-step stone staircase climb from Tikhedhunga to Ulleri (2,073 m). This is one of the most challenging short ascents on the Annapurna trail — take it steady and enjoy the rhododendron and oak forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Ulleri through Banthanti to Ghorepani (2,874 m). The trail passes through dense rhododendron forest — in October the foliage is rich and green. Arrive at Ghorepani in early afternoon and check into your teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the village of Ghorepani, meet fellow trekkers, and enjoy views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South from the village viewpoints. Rest early in preparation for the pre-dawn Poon Hill hike.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey, boiled eggs, and butter tea at Tikhedhunga teahouse, NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a teahouse in Ulleri, NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dal bhat (unlimited refills) at Ghorepani teahouse — the trekker's staple, NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: The Tikhedhunga to Ulleri staircase is steep — use trekking poles. October weather is typically clear and mild (10–18°C at Ghorepani). Nights can be cold — have a warm sleeping bag liner ready.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn start (4:30–5:00 AM) for the 45-minute hike to Poon Hill (3,210 m) to witness one of Nepal's most spectacular sunrises over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. On a clear October morning, you'll see Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and Dhaulagiri glowing in alpenglow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for breakfast, then trek onward through Deurali to Tadapani (2,630 m) — a 4–5 hour moderate hike through rhododendron and magnolia forest with excellent mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tadapani and enjoy panoramic views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) and Annapurna South from the village clearing. Relax and journal about the day's highlights.

meals.breakfast: Hot ginger tea and biscuits on Poon Hill summit, then a full cooked breakfast back at Ghorepani teahouse — pancakes, eggs, and coffee, NPR 500–700
meals.lunch: Light snacks and energy bars on the trail between Deurali and Tadapani
meals.dinner: Garlic soup (altitude remedy), vegetable pasta or dal bhat at Tadapani teahouse, NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headlamp, warm layers, and a camera for Poon Hill. Arrive by 5:30 AM to secure a good viewing spot — it gets crowded in October peak season. The Tadapani trail has some steep sections after Deurali.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani down through dense forest to Chhomrong (2,170 m) — approximately 4–5 hours. The trail descends steeply and then climbs back up through terraced fields and the Gurung village of Chhomrong, one of the largest villages on the Annapurna Sanctuary route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chhomrong village, visit the local school and gompa (Buddhist monastery), and enjoy sweeping views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Chhomrong marks the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary (ABC) trail.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the teahouse culture in Chhomrong — this is one of the best-equipped villages on the route. Hot showers available (NPR 200–300 extra). Celebrate reaching the Sanctuary gateway.

meals.breakfast: Muesli with warm milk, toast with peanut butter at Tadapani teahouse, NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or pasta at a teahouse in Sinuwa (midway stop), NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Apple pie (Chhomrong is famous for it!), vegetable curry, and masala tea at a Chhomrong teahouse, NPR 600–900

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong has reliable WiFi and charging facilities — a good point to update family back home. Stock up on snacks and water purification tablets here as prices increase higher up. The descent to Chhomrong involves many stone steps — take care on knees.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down the long staircase, cross the Chhomrong Khola river, and begin the climb through Sinuwa and into the bamboo and rhododendron forest toward Bamboo (2,310 m). The trail enters the Annapurna Conservation Area's inner sanctuary zone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Bamboo through Dovan to Himalaya Hotel (2,920 m) — passing through increasingly dramatic gorge scenery with waterfalls and towering cliffs. The Modi Khola river roars alongside the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the Himalaya Hotel teahouse — one of the more comfortable mid-route stops. The surrounding forest and river sounds create a magical atmosphere. Spot Himalayan tahr (wild mountain goat) on the cliffs above.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and boiled eggs at Chhomrong teahouse, NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Bamboo teahouse, NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with vegetable curry and hot lemon tea at Himalaya Hotel, NPR 700–900

day_by_day.notes: The trail between Chhomrong and Himalaya Hotel passes through avalanche zones — stay on the marked path and do not linger in exposed areas. Prices for food and accommodation increase significantly from here onward. Carry enough cash (no ATMs beyond Chhomrong).

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel through Hinku Cave (a natural rock overhang used as shelter) to Deurali (3,230 m). The trail narrows and the landscape becomes more alpine — views of Machhapuchhre's south face begin to dominate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the dramatic ascent from Deurali into the Annapurna Sanctuary — the valley opens up suddenly into a vast glacial amphitheater. Trek to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700 m. Arrive at MBC and take in the awe-inspiring 360-degree mountain panorama.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from MBC — Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Annapurna I, Annapurna III, Gangapurna, and Hiunchuli glow in the fading light. This is one of Nepal's most iconic mountain views. Rest and hydrate well for the ABC push tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, boiled eggs, and ginger tea at Himalaya Hotel, NPR 500–700
meals.lunch: Noodle soup and chocolate bar at Deurali teahouse, NPR 600–800
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta with garlic soup at MBC teahouse — garlic helps with altitude, NPR 800–1,100

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness risk increases significantly above 3,000 m. Watch for symptoms: headache, nausea, dizziness, loss of appetite. Drink 3–4 liters of water daily. Carry Diamox if prescribed. MBC nights are very cold (0 to -5°C) — use all available blankets and your sleeping bag liner.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 4:30 AM and trek the final 2 hours from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130 m. Arrive at sunrise to witness the full Annapurna Sanctuary amphitheater illuminated — Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, Annapurna III, and Machhapuchhre surrounding you in a complete mountain circle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon at ABC — explore the glacial moraine, visit the memorial plaques for mountaineers, take photographs, and simply absorb the extraordinary high-altitude environment. Begin the descent back to MBC or Deurali after lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Continue descent to Deurali or push back to Himalaya Hotel (3–4 hours total descent). Celebrate reaching ABC with a well-deserved hot meal and rest.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea, biscuits, and energy bars at MBC before the pre-dawn start
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or instant noodles at ABC teahouse — the highest meal of the trip!, NPR 900–1,200
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry, soup, and hot chocolate at Deurali or Himalaya Hotel teahouse, NPR 700–1,000

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire trek — cherish every moment at ABC. At 4,130 m, move slowly and breathe deeply. Do not rush the descent — descend only as far as you feel comfortable. October is peak season so teahouses fill quickly — the guide/porter can radio ahead to reserve space.

day_by_day.morning: Full descent day — trek from overnight stop (Himalaya Hotel or Deurali) back through Bamboo, Sinuwa, and up the Chhomrong staircase. The descent is long but the body adjusts well as altitude decreases. Enjoy the returning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at Chhomrong by early afternoon — enjoy a well-deserved hot shower and rest. Visit the Chhomrong Eco-Tourism Center to learn about the Gurung community's conservation efforts in the Annapurna region.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Chhomrong — you've completed the ABC trek! Enjoy the teahouse's best offerings and share stories with fellow trekkers. Reflect on the journey with a cup of masala chai.

meals.breakfast: Porridge, pancakes, and tea at your overnight teahouse, NPR 500–700
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Bamboo or Sinuwa teahouse, NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Celebratory dal bhat thali with dessert (apple pie or chocolate cake) at Chhomrong, NPR 700–1,000

day_by_day.notes: The Chhomrong staircase on the return is a knee-killer — use trekking poles and take it slowly. Your body will be tired after 8 days of trekking — listen to it and rest whenever needed. Chhomrong is a good place to tip your guide and porter if you're satisfied with their service.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back to Jhinu Danda (1,780 m) — a 2-hour descent through terraced fields and forest. Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs beside the Modi Khola river.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Jhinu Danda natural hot springs — a perfect reward after 9 days of trekking. The thermal pools beside the roaring river are a magical experience. Spend 1–2 hours relaxing in the healing waters (entry fee approx. NPR 200–300).
day_by_day.evening: Trek from Jhinu Danda down to Nayapul (3–4 hours) or stay overnight at Jhinu Danda and complete the exit the next morning. If returning to Pokhara today, take a local bus or jeep from Nayapul (2 hours to Pokhara).

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at Chhomrong teahouse — eggs any style, toast, and coffee, NPR 500–700
meals.lunch: Light snack or dal bhat at Jhinu Danda teahouse, NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Arrive in Pokhara and enjoy a well-earned restaurant meal at a Lakeside restaurant — try Nepali set menu or wood-fired pizza, NPR 800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs at Jhinu Danda are one of the best-kept secrets of the Annapurna trek — do not skip them! If arriving in Pokhara in the evening, book your hotel in advance as October is peak season and Lakeside fills up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in late, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and do gentle stretching or yoga. Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (entry NPR 300) — an excellent museum dedicated to the Himalayas, mountaineering history, and Nepali mountain culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a rowboat or kayak on Phewa Lake (NPR 300–500/hour) and paddle to the Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake. Alternatively, take a short hike up to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic views of Pokhara, Phewa Lake, and the Annapurna range.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pokhara's Lakeside (Baidam) area — browse handicraft shops, buy souvenirs, and enjoy the vibrant café culture. Watch the sunset over Phewa Lake from a lakeside restaurant terrace.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent breakfast at a Lakeside café — fresh fruit bowl, granola, eggs Benedict, and fresh-pressed juice, NPR 600–900
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Lakeside restaurant — try Newari set meal or thukpa (Tibetan noodle soup), NPR 600–900
meals.dinner: Dinner at Beam Bar & Restaurant or OR2K Restaurant — international and Nepali fusion cuisine, NPR 800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Your legs will be sore after the trek — gentle walking only today. Get a traditional Nepali massage at a Lakeside spa (NPR 1,500–2,500 for 60–90 minutes) to aid muscle recovery. Recharge your electronics and back up all your trek photos.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise drive or taxi to Sarangkot viewpoint (1,592 m) — 30 minutes from Pokhara — for spectacular dawn views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges from a different perspective than Poon Hill. The views of Machhapuchhre, Annapurna I, II, III, and IV are outstanding on clear October mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara and visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave and Davis Falls — two natural wonders located near the airport. The cave contains a sacred Shiva shrine deep inside its chambers. Then visit the Tibetan Refugee Camp at Tashiling to learn about Tibetan culture and browse handmade carpets and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Nepali cultural dinner show — several Lakeside restaurants offer live Nepali folk music and dance performances while you dine. A wonderful way to experience Nepali culture beyond the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and snacks at Sarangkot viewpoint, then full breakfast back in Pokhara, NPR 500–700
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Nepali restaurant away from the tourist strip — try a local bhansa ghar (home kitchen) for authentic dal bhat, NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Cultural dinner at Pokhara's Lakeside with live Gurung/Magar folk music — Nepali thali set meal, NPR 1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: Sarangkot is also a popular paragliding launch site — if you're interested in paragliding over Pokhara and Phewa Lake, this is the day to book it (USD 80–120 for a 30-minute tandem flight). Book in advance during October peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Optional: Take an early morning flight back to Kathmandu (25 minutes) or travel by tourist bus (6–7 hours). Upon arrival in Kathmandu, check into a mid-range hotel in Thamel. Then visit the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Pashupatinath Temple — the most sacred Hindu temple in Nepal — and witness the evening Aarti ceremony preparations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Boudhanath Stupa — one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walk the kora (circumambulation path) around the stupa with pilgrims and monks, visit the Tibetan monasteries surrounding it, and browse the thangka painting shops.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Thamel — Kathmandu's vibrant traveler district. Shop for trekking souvenirs, Nepali handicrafts, pashmina scarves, and thangka paintings. Enjoy a farewell dinner at one of Thamel's excellent restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Pokhara hotel or on the tourist bus, NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Lunch near Boudhanath — try a Tibetan restaurant for momos (dumplings) and butter tea, NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Chez Caroline or Thamel House Restaurant — fine Nepali cuisine in a heritage setting, NPR 1,200–1,800

day_by_day.notes: Book your Kathmandu hotel in Thamel in advance — October is peak tourist season and good mid-range hotels fill up quickly. Keep your ACAP and TIMS permits as souvenirs. The Pashupatinath evening Aarti ceremony begins around 6:00 PM and is deeply moving.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal — visit Swayambhunath Stupa (Monkey Temple) at sunrise for panoramic views over the Kathmandu Valley and a final spiritual experience. The hilltop stupa is one of Nepal's oldest religious sites and offers a peaceful farewell to the country.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kathmandu Durbar Square (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — explore the ancient royal palace complex, Kumari Ghar (home of the Living Goddess), and the intricate Newari architecture. Do any final souvenir shopping in the old bazaars around Durbar Square.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 3 hours early for international departures. Carry all trekking permits and receipts for customs if required. Depart Nepal with extraordinary memories of the Annapurna Sanctuary.

meals.breakfast: Final Nepali breakfast at your Thamel hotel — sel roti (rice doughnut), aloo tarkari (potato curry), and masala tea, NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Thamel café before airport transfer — sandwiches or momos, NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant meal or carry snacks for the flight

day_by_day.notes: Nepal's Tribhuvan International Airport can be congested — allow extra time for check-in and security. Nepali Rupees cannot be exchanged outside Nepal — convert remaining NPR back to your currency at the airport bank before departure. Carry trekking permits, hotel receipts, and any purchased handicraft certificates (for customs). Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Modi Khola Valley Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Kathmandu airport to your boutique stay in the Modi Khola Valley, Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy a scenic drive through the Nepalese countryside with a personal guide narrating the landscape, culture, and upcoming trek highlights. Check-in and settle into your premium accommodation with a welcome refreshment and orientation briefing.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle acclimatization stroll around the immediate lodge surroundings, breathing in the crisp mountain air and absorbing the first views of the Annapurna massif at dusk. Return for a curated welcome dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light gourmet snack box provided during private transfer
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the boutique lodge — multi-course Nepali tasting menu featuring dal bhat, lamb sekuwa, seasonal vegetables, and artisan raksi or premium Himalayan wine

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all trekking permits (ACAP and TIMS) are confirmed with your guide upon arrival. Hydrate well and avoid strenuous activity on Day 1 to begin acclimatization. Altitude at Modi Khola Valley base is approximately 1,100m.

day_by_day.morning: Post-breakfast guided nature walk along the Modi Khola riverbank, exploring the subtropical forest ecosystem, spotting exotic bird species including Himalayan monals and rufous-bellied eagles. Your private naturalist guide provides detailed insights into local flora and fauna.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby traditional Gurung village for an immersive cultural experience — tour ancient stone homes, observe millet harvesting, and participate in a hands-on thangka painting demonstration with a local artisan.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga and meditation session on the lodge's private terrace overlooking the valley, led by a resident wellness instructor. Followed by a curated cocktail hour with Himalayan herbal infusions and canapés.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet lodge breakfast — fresh Himalayan honey, buckwheat pancakes, eggs to order, seasonal fruit, and Nepali masala tea
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at the Gurung village — traditional sel roti, aloo tama curry, and fresh buttermilk
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the lodge — roasted chicken with timur pepper sauce, sautéed fiddlehead ferns, and warm chocolate fondant with cardamom cream

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the village visit. Carry a light jacket for the evening session. This day is designed as a gentle introduction before trekking begins.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided trek from the lodge toward Nayapul or Birethanti (depending on starting point), following the lower Annapurna trail through lush rhododendron and oak forests. The trail offers stunning views of Hiunchuli and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking upward to Tikhedhunga or Ulleri, gaining altitude gradually. Rest at a premium teahouse with a private room reserved for a hot lunch and foot massage service arranged by your concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a pre-booked luxury teahouse lodge in Ulleri or Ghorepani foothills. Enjoy a hot stone bath, followed by a briefing on tomorrow's Poon Hill ascent.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — granola, yogurt, toast with local jam, and ginger lemon tea
meals.lunch: Hot soup, grilled yak cheese sandwich, and fresh juice at premium teahouse stop
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at luxury teahouse lodge — garlic soup, pasta with local mushrooms, and apple pie with custard

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance approximately 8–10 km. Altitude gain to ~2,000m. Trekking poles recommended. Your porter will carry main luggage; carry a day pack with essentials.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn guided ascent to Poon Hill (3,210m) to witness one of the most iconic sunrises in the Himalayas — panoramic views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre illuminated in golden alpenglow. Private photography session with a professional mountain photographer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to lodge for a hearty brunch, then continue trekking through rhododendron forests toward Tadapani, enjoying sweeping valley views and dense forest canopy.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tadapani luxury lodge. Enjoy a private bonfire with roasted chestnuts and Himalayan herbal tea. Stargazing session with a telescope provided by the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-dawn energy snack — energy bars, thermos of hot tea provided at Poon Hill
meals.lunch: Full brunch back at lodge — eggs benedict, fresh fruit platter, and Nepali coffee
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Tadapani lodge — slow-braised lamb with Himalayan spices, roasted root vegetables, and Kheer (rice pudding) with saffron

day_by_day.notes: Wake-up call at 04:00 for Poon Hill ascent. Temperature at Poon Hill can drop to near freezing — wear thermal layers and a down jacket. The professional photographer package should be pre-arranged with the tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani through dense mixed forests toward Chhomrong, crossing suspension bridges over roaring mountain streams. The trail offers dramatic views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Birdwatching opportunities abound in this biodiversity corridor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong, a picturesque Gurung village perched on a hillside. Explore the village, visit the local gompa (monastery), and enjoy a private guided cultural interaction with a Gurung elder sharing oral traditions and folklore.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at your premium Chhomrong lodge with a deep-tissue massage by a trained therapist. Enjoy the terrace views of Annapurna South as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — porridge with honey and nuts, boiled eggs, and masala tea
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch enjoyed on a scenic viewpoint — smoked salmon wrap, trail mix, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at Chhomrong lodge — vegetable thukpa (noodle soup), steamed momos with sesame dipping sauce, and warm brownie with vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance approximately 10–12 km with significant elevation changes. Chhomrong sits at approximately 2,170m. Ensure trekking permits are checked at the Chhomrong checkpoint.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong descending to Sinuwa, then ascending through bamboo and rhododendron forests toward Bamboo and Dovan. The forest becomes increasingly dense and atmospheric — watch for langur monkeys and Himalayan black bears in the undergrowth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Himalaya Hotel area toward Deurali. The trail narrows as you enter the Annapurna Sanctuary corridor. A private guide narrates the geological and ecological significance of the sanctuary zone.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a premium lodge at Deurali or Himalaya Hotel. Enjoy a restorative herbal foot soak and a warm dinner by the fire.

meals.breakfast: Hearty lodge breakfast — banana pancakes, peanut butter toast, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Hot lunch at Bamboo teahouse — dal bhat with seasonal vegetables and buttermilk
meals.dinner: Dinner at Deurali lodge — hearty lentil soup, grilled chicken with garlic butter, and caramel pudding

day_by_day.notes: This section of the trail can be misty and cool — pack a rain cover for your daypack. Altitude at Deurali is approximately 3,230m. Begin watching for signs of altitude sickness and stay well hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Deurali through the dramatic glacial moraine landscape toward Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m. The trail opens up spectacularly as you enter the Annapurna Sanctuary amphitheater — surrounded on all sides by 7,000m+ peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at MBC and take time to absorb the extraordinary 360-degree mountain panorama. Short exploratory walk around the base camp area with your guide explaining the glaciology and mountaineering history of the region.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from MBC — watch the peaks turn pink and orange in the alpenglow. Private champagne toast at altitude to celebrate reaching the sanctuary. Early dinner and rest for the final push to ABC tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Energy-rich breakfast — oatmeal with dried fruits, scrambled eggs, and hot chocolate
meals.lunch: Packed luxury lunch at a scenic rest point — quinoa salad, protein bars, and thermos soup
meals.dinner: Warm dinner at MBC lodge — vegetable fried rice, tomato soup, and chocolate mousse

day_by_day.notes: Altitude at MBC is 3,700m — acclimatization is critical. Move slowly, drink 3–4 liters of water, and avoid alcohol except for the ceremonial toast. Altitude medication (Diamox) should be discussed with your guide and physician in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning ascent from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — the crown jewel of the itinerary. Arrive at ABC as the morning light bathes Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, and the iconic Machhapuchhre in brilliant gold. Private professional photography session at ABC.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore ABC and its surroundings with your guide — learn about the history of Annapurna expeditions, the first 8,000m peak ever summited (1950, French expedition). Meditative solo time to absorb the magnitude of the landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at ABC — one of the most dramatic mountain sunsets on earth. Private gourmet dinner at the ABC lodge to celebrate the achievement. Toast with premium Himalayan spirits.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-trek snack — energy bars and hot tea before departure from MBC
meals.lunch: Special celebratory lunch at ABC — gourmet packed meal with premium items including artisan cheese, charcuterie, crackers, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Celebratory premium dinner at ABC lodge — chef's special multi-course meal including mushroom bisque, herb-crusted chicken, and a special summit cake

day_by_day.notes: This is the highest point of the itinerary at 4,130m. Take it slow, rest frequently, and communicate any symptoms of altitude sickness immediately to your guide. The achievement of reaching ABC deserves to be savored — allow ample time for reflection and photography.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise at ABC — a deeply spiritual and awe-inspiring experience. Guided meditation session at the base camp with the mountains as your backdrop. Begin descent toward MBC and Deurali, retracing the sanctuary trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descent through the bamboo forest zone toward Bamboo or Sinuwa. The descent is significantly faster — enjoy the changing vegetation as altitude drops and the air grows richer.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a comfortable lodge in Sinuwa or Chhomrong area. Enjoy a hot shower, a well-earned massage, and a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at ABC — hot porridge, boiled eggs, and Himalayan herbal tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bamboo or Dovan teahouse — noodle soup, spring rolls, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sinuwa or Chhomrong lodge — dal bhat set with all accompaniments, and kheer dessert

day_by_day.notes: Descend carefully — knees take significant strain on steep downhill sections. Trekking poles are highly recommended. Celebrate the achievement but maintain focus on safe descent.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong or Sinuwa back toward Jhinu Danda, famous for its natural hot springs on the banks of the Modi Khola river. The trail winds through terraced farmland with stunning valley views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jhinu Danda and descend to the natural hot springs — a perfect therapeutic reward after days of high-altitude trekking. Private hot spring session arranged for your group. Your concierge will have towels, robes, and refreshments waiting.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a premium lodge near Jhinu Danda. Enjoy a sunset dinner overlooking the river gorge.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — French toast with maple syrup, fresh fruit, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the trail — gourmet sandwiches, fruit, and energy snacks
meals.dinner: Dinner at Jhinu Danda lodge — grilled fish from Modi Khola, roasted potatoes, and mango kulfi

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs at Jhinu Danda are a highlight — water temperature is naturally warm and the riverside setting is magical. Bring a swimsuit and flip-flops. The descent to the springs from the village takes about 20 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning trek back toward the Modi Khola Valley base area and your boutique lodge. The return journey offers a reflective opportunity to appreciate the full arc of the Annapurna Sanctuary experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your Modi Khola Valley boutique stay. Full afternoon of luxury recovery — spa treatments including deep tissue massage, aromatherapy, and a private plunge pool session. Personal debrief with your guide over afternoon tea.
day_by_day.evening: Private guided sunset hike to a nearby viewpoint for final Annapurna range panoramas. Return for a premium farewell dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — eggs benedict, granola parfait, fresh juice, and Nepali coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the lodge — avocado toast, Caesar salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner — five-course tasting menu featuring the best of Nepali and continental cuisine, paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery day — allow your body to rest after the high-altitude trek. Drink plenty of fluids and eat well to replenish energy reserves. Arrange any souvenir shopping or special requests with the lodge concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided day hike to a lesser-known viewpoint in the Modi Khola Valley — off the main trekking routes for an exclusive, crowd-free experience. Your naturalist guide leads a deep-dive nature walk focusing on medicinal plants and traditional Gurung herbal knowledge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm and participate in a premium farm-to-table cooking class — learn to prepare traditional Nepali dishes using fresh local ingredients, guided by a professional chef.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class for dinner on the lodge terrace. Private bonfire and storytelling session with a local cultural guide sharing Gurung mythology and Himalayan folklore.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — buckwheat crepes with honey, fresh berries, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at the viewpoint — charcuterie board, artisan cheeses, crackers, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the cooking class — dal bhat, vegetable curry, sel roti, and homemade achar, enjoyed on the terrace

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a wonderful way to take a piece of Nepal home with you. Request a recipe card from the chef. This day is intentionally relaxed to allow full physical recovery before the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning sunrise yoga and meditation session at the lodge, overlooking the Annapurna range. Reflect on the journey with your wellness instructor. Pack and prepare for departure to Kathmandu.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Modi Khola Valley back to Kathmandu. Stop en route at Pokhara for a scenic lakeside lunch by Phewa Lake — one of Nepal's most beautiful settings. Optional short boat ride on the lake with views of the Annapurna range reflected in the water.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Kathmandu and check into a luxury 5-star hotel (e.g., Dwarika's Hotel or Hyatt Regency Kathmandu). Freshen up and enjoy a premium dinner in Kathmandu's finest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast — full spread including eggs, pastries, fruit, and Nepali tea
meals.lunch: Premium lakeside lunch in Pokhara — fresh trout from Phewa Lake, risotto, and dessert at a top Pokhara restaurant
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Kathmandu — contemporary Nepali cuisine at Dwarika's Krishnarpan restaurant or equivalent, multi-course tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara stopover is approximately 1.5–2 hours. Ensure luggage is loaded in the private vehicle before the morning departure. Confirm Kathmandu hotel check-in details with your concierge in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kathmandu — private guided tour of UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Pashupatinath Temple and Boudhanath Stupa. A deeply spiritual and culturally enriching conclusion to the journey. Professional guide provides historical and religious context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping in Thamel and Durbar Marg — premium Nepali handicrafts, pashmina shawls, thangka paintings, and Himalayan crystals. Your personal shopping guide assists in identifying authentic, high-quality items. Final spa treatment at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell premium dinner at the hotel or a top Kathmandu restaurant. Private transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for departure flight. Depart Nepal with extraordinary memories of the Annapurna Sanctuary.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — full international and Nepali buffet spread
meals.lunch: Light gourmet lunch in Thamel — at a premium café, featuring continental and Nepali fusion dishes
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — premium restaurant in Kathmandu featuring Newari cuisine, live traditional music, and a curated dessert selection

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details and airport transfer timing with your concierge the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Ensure all purchased items comply with customs regulations. A truly extraordinary 14-day premium Annapurna experience concludes today.
